text: RLS filters only flow one direction by default — even across a relationship that's otherwise bidirectional.
One checkbox turns that on, per relationship. Reach for it specifically when dynamic RLS needs it — not as a general fix.

One real constraint: a table in several bidirectional relationships can only have security filtering in both directions turned on for one of them. And the real cost is performance — it can slow queries meaningfully in large, related models, so test thoroughly before trusting it anywhere real.
Test as role isn't limited to one report — switch and check every report built on the same semantic model, not just the first one.
That closes Chapter Eleven, and everything this course teaches about securing a semantic model on purpose. Chapter Twelve puts all of it together in one capstone project.
